authoredSolutions.51: Write \(x=n+t\) with \(n=[x]\), \(t\in[0,1)\), so \(4x+2[x]=6n+4t\). The domain of \(\cos^{-1}\) needs \(-3\le 6n+4t\le 3\). For \(n=0\): \(t\in[0,\tfrac34]\), i.e. \(x\in[0,\tfrac34]\). For \(n=-1\): \(t\in[\tfrac34,1)\), i.e. \(x\in[-\tfrac14,0)\). No other \(n\) works, so the domain is \([-\tfrac14,\tfrac34]\). Thus \(\alpha+\beta=\tfrac12\) and \(12(\alpha+\beta)=6\).

Its real part is \(\dfrac{y}{y-1}\) and imaginary part \(\dfrac{-3}{y-1}\); for \(\arg=\tfrac{\pi}{4}\) both are positive and equal, so \(-\tfrac3y=1\Rightarrow y=-3\).
